message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills, modern scares, and some hidden gems you might enjoy for a Friday‑night movie marathon:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel, featuring Jack Nicholson’s iconic descent into madness. |
| 2 | **Get Out** (2017) | A smart blend of horror and social satire that keeps you guessing until the very end. |
| 3 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A slow‑burn family drama that turns into a nightmare; the dread builds beautifully. |
| 4 | **Midsommar** (2019) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations—think “The Wicker Man” meets Wes Craven. |
| 5 | **It Follows** (2014) | A fresh take on the supernatural chase genre with a creepy, relentless vibe. |
| 6 | **The Babadook** (2014) | An Australian indie that uses a child‑monster metaphor to explore grief and mental illness. |
| 7 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Suspenseful, low‑talk, high‑heart‑rate; the silence itself becomes terrifying. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | A well‑crafted paranormal investigation that balances jump‑scares with atmosphere. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | Dario Argento’s color‑splashed ballet of terror—great for fans of surreal visuals. |
|10 | **The Others** (2001) | A gothic mystery with Nicole Kidman that delivers a twisty, atmospheric experience. |

Feel free to shuffle them or pick a theme (e.g., “classic vs. contemporary”) depending on your mood. Enjoy the fright!
